To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spatial part-whole relationships between spatial objects can be modeled by extending the Unified Modeling Language with spatial constructs.

(1) the PW relationships between spatial objects are classified into three different types—spatial part (e.g., the division of an area into zones), spatial membership (e.g., a person living in a zone), and spatial inclusion (e.g., an area included in a larger area); and (2) the modeling constructs supporting the PW relationships can be added to the UML for spatiotemporally extended data.

We propose a practical approach to modeling part-whole relationships between spatial objects using a classification framework based on derivation and constraint relationships, which is integrated with an existing modeling language.

developing a formal approach to modeling spatial part-whole relationships in conceptual modeling languages.
providing conceptual modeling constructs that support PW relationships for spatial applications, and we demonstrate that such constructs are possible using the Extended Spatiotempo-ral UML.
